correctness.rationale: The source utility has exactly 0<q=p(1/3)=p(2/3)<1=p(1/2) on attainable fractions. Nonsegregated agents cannot strictly benefit from moving into the lone vacancy. The three vacancy-neighbor cases therefore give exact equilibrium criteria; blue runs of length at most two yield the sharp lower DoI b+ceil(b/2)+1 and an attained construction. Counting at most two red neighbors per blue proves min(n,3b) upper optimum, attained in the balanced, intermediate and red-excess ranges. For r=b=1, DoI=2. Exact brute force compares every placement and strict jump for small n as supplemental checks, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact ratio classifies the strategic loss of integration for all population sizes in the particularly motivated one-vacancy cycle class that is known to have convergence and PoS=1. It quantifies the gap between a potential game reaching some equilibrium and the quality of its worst equilibrium, with natural imbalance/size dependence, explicit attained constructions and a limiting sharp value 2. This is a complete finite-parameter classification rather than a routine restatement of the general bound.
